writeup.headline: Texas Instruments rates Buy on strong growth, quality and momentum, but a demanding valuation keeps it near Hold.
writeup.thesis: TXN scores 66, just 2 points above the Hold line, so the Buy rating rests on a narrow margin. Growth is strong, with TTM revenue growth of 20.3% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 27.7% year on year, and growth sped up by 4.9 pp from the previous quarter. Quality and the balance sheet are solid: a 60.2% gross margin, a 40.8% operating margin, a normalised FCF margin of 20.5% and net debt at 0.74x FCF. The share price trend is strong, with the price 19.9% above its 200-day average and shares 7.2 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation is the main drag (score 19). In absolute terms the multiples are high at 13.6x sales, 66.4x normalised FCF and 34.1x EBIT, and the stock is expensive against its own history, with P/S more expensive than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: High absolute valuation: FCF yield 3.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield and P/S of 13.6x leave little room for disappointment.
The Q4 revenue outlook of $5.80–6.30B implies a slight sequential decline, which could slow the growth momentum.
Reported FCF margin of 35.2% versus 12.1% a year earlier may not last; the normalised margin is 20.5%.
After a strong run, with shares up 70.6% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, the stock is exposed to a pullback in semiconductor sentiment.
Three directors filed Form 144 notices of proposed sales totalling about $4.5M after earnings, and no insider purchases were found.
what_would_change: A drop of just 2 points in the score, for example from weaker trend or news scores, would move the rating to Hold.
Slowing revenue growth or margin pressure in the next quarter would weigh on the growth and quality scores and could push the rating down.
Reaching Strong Buy at 80 would need 14 more points, most plausibly from a sharp improvement in the valuation score, such as a lower price or much higher earnings and FCF.
